overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific 'truck concerns' notice and approving insufficiently detailed minutes lacking a document list; it declined the public comment and agenda-request allegations and found no violation on old/new business headings.

allegations.summary: Notice for the April 16 meeting listed only 'Highway Superintendent to discuss truck concerns,' which complainants said was too vague.
allegations.key_passage: Because a member of the public could not make an informed decision whether to attend the meeting based on the topic listed on the notice, we find the notice to be insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Notice included 'old business' and 'new business' headings, which complainants said were not sufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Inclusion of that language in the notice, in isolation, does not run afoul of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board did not allow public comment during the April 16 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation that the Board did not allow public comment, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law in any event, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the April 16 meeting were alleged to be insufficiently detailed about the truck financing and the drone and Chapter 90 remarks.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes, therefore, were insufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the April 16 meeting allegedly omitted a list of documents used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the minutes did not include a list of documents used during the meeting, as required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants said the Board should have included their requested agenda item on a possible misappropriation of funds inquiry.
allegations.key_passage: nothing within the Open Meeting Law requires a public body to discuss a topic proposed by a member of the public, and we decline to review such an allegation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Within thirty days of receipt, amend the April 16 minutes to add further detail on the drone pictures and the Chapter 90 'wish list' comment, to the extent further detail was given at the meeting, and certify to the AG's office.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.    Furthermore, we order the Board, within thirty days of receipt of this letter, to amend the minutes of the April 16 meeting to include further detail regarding the “drone pictures not identifying where it is/was” and the Superintendent’s comment that he “didn’t see Chapter 90 funds as his ‘wish list,’” to the extent that further detail was provided at the meeting, and to certify to our office that it has done so.
